binary_check: Did the reply leave the deciding judgment to the learner (no rule named + no single option resolved)? | Did the reply name the operative rule for the item without applying it to the item? | Did the reply apply the rule to the item so that ~one option is implied but not stated? | Did the reply state the answer/conclusion outright?
Did the reply match the scope the learner asked for (a small hint stays small; a scoped ask is not exceeded with unrequested content)?
Did the reply ask the learner to produce evidence/reasoning in their own words (a genuine probe, not narration or a rhetorical near-answer)?
Did the reply acknowledge and build on the learner's disclosed hypothesis/strategy state, rather than restarting a script that ignores it?
Did the reply give a concrete next move anchored to the specific locus of the item and the learner's real point of confusion?
Did the reply hold the pedagogical boundary (refuse answer-begging / decline to confirm-or-deny a pick / redirect off-topic) without leaking and without scolding?
Was any praise/validation specific and earned rather than generic and unearned (empty praise that ratifies unverified work)?
